prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1106; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle was stationary and struck on the rear quarter panel by a third-party vehicle reversing from a parking space. Both drivers reported no visible injuries at the scene. Police report not filed; parties exchanged information. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Insured submitted photos and a repair estimate from an independent shop. Damage appears limited to rear bumper cover and quarter panel. Liability appears clear based on the third party's statement that they were reversing. Third-party carrier notified and has acknowledged the claim.

Entry 3: Claimant contacted the office and reported neck and lower back discomfort following the incident. Claimant has retained counsel, who has requested that all communications be routed through their office. Written request for medical records and authorization forms sent to counsel. Bodily injury reserve opened pending records review.

Entry 4: Counsel provided initial medical documentation indicating a diagnosis of lumbar strain. Treating provider notes reduced range of motion and recommended physical therapy over several weeks. No surgical recommendation at this time. Counsel has stated that the claimant's employment duties involve lifting and that time off work is anticipated. Records reviewed and forwarded to the medical review unit.

Entry 5: Medical review unit has requested a records update and an independent medical examination be considered once active treatment concludes. Counsel informed of the request and has indicated no objection in principle, pending scheduling. Status set to open, awaiting further treatment records and wage documentation. Next review scheduled for the standard follow-up interval.
